# SurveyNCD: Survey-Weighted Analysis of Self-Reported Health Indicators

**SurveyNCD** provides specialized tools for analysing population health
survey data from the World Health Organization (WHO) Stepwise Approach
to Non-Communicable Disease (NCD) Risk Factor Surveillance (STEPS),
Demographic and Health Surveys (DHS), Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys
(MICS), and similar complex sample surveys.

In population surveys, chronic conditions are typically self-reported
rather than coded using the International Classification of Diseases
(ICD). Standard statistical functions (like
[`mean()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/mean.html) or unweighted regression)
produce biased estimates and misleading p-values because they ignore the
survey design. **SurveyNCD** bridges this gap by accounting for
stratification, clustering (PSUs), and sampling weights throughout the
analytical workflow.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Installation

### Released version from CRAN (Recommended)

You can install the published version directly from
[CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=SurveyNCD):

``` r

install.packages("SurveyNCD")
```

### Development version from GitHub

To install the latest development build from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("StatAid-Research-Lab/SurveyNCD")
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What SurveyNCD does

Four steps cover a typical analysis: build the design once, clean and
score the answers, estimate, then report.

| Step | Functions |
|----|----|
| **1. Design** | [`dhs_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md), [`mics_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md), [`steps_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md): the correct design from each programme’s standard variable names (or any `survey`/`srvyr` design) |
| **2. Clean and score** | [`recode_binary()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/recode_binary.md) (1/2/9 or text codes to 0/1/NA), [`multimorbidity_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/multimorbidity_index.md) (condition count, adjustable threshold), [`fci_items()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/fci_items.md), [`who_anthro_score()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/who_anthro_score.md) (DHS-coded child z-scores) |
| **3. Estimate** | [`survey_prevalence()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_prevalence.md) (any binary indicators, several grouping variables), [`mm_prevalence()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_prevalence.md), [`mm_standardize()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_standardize.md) with [`who_standard_population()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/who_standard_population.md) (age standardisation), [`mm_patterns()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_patterns.md) (pairs and triads, observed/expected), [`mm_bounds()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_bounds.md) (“don’t know” sensitivity bounds) |
| **4. Inequality** | [`survey_concentration_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_concentration_index.md) (standard, generalized, Erreygers, Wagstaff; by group), [`survey_concentration_curve()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_concentration_curve.md), [`survey_slope_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_slope_index.md) (SII and RII) |
| **Report** | [`ncd_table()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/ncd_table.md) (publication-ready table), `autoplot()` methods for every result |
| *Experimental* | [`survey_map_indicator()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_map_indicator.md), [`survey_xgboost()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_xgboost.md), [`survey_shap()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_shap.md), [`plot_shap_summary()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/plot_shap_summary.md) |

All variance estimation is done by the
[survey](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=survey) package, so every
standard error reflects strata, clusters and weights. Each estimator is
tested against an independent calculation.

> **Experimental functions.** The machine-learning functions apply
> sampling weights as case weights but do not carry strata and clusters
> into any measure of uncertainty. Use them to explore patterns, not for
> inference. Their interface may change.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Quick start

``` r

library(SurveyNCD)

d <- ncd_survey                                   # simulated STEPS-style data
d$htn <- recode_binary(d$htn_raw, yes = 1, no = 2)
d$dm  <- recode_binary(d$dm_raw,  yes = 1, no = 2)
d$dep <- recode_binary(d$dep_raw, yes = "Yes", no = "No")
d <- multimorbidity_index(d, c("htn", "dm", "dep"), na_action = "na")

des <- steps_design(d, weight = "wt")             # psu / stratum / weight

ncd_table(des, c("htn", "dm", "dep"), by = "sex")             # formatted table
survey_prevalence(des, "htn", by = c("sex", "residence"))     # numbers behind it
mm_prevalence(des, by = "residence")                          # multimorbidity
mm_patterns(des, c("htn", "dm", "dep"))                       # common pairs
survey_concentration_index(des, dm, wealth_score, type = "erreygers")
ggplot2::autoplot(survey_concentration_curve(des, dm, wealth_score))
```

With DHS data:

``` r

des <- dhs_design(ir_data)    # PSU v021, strata v023, weight v005 / 1e6
```

## Example data and a complete worked analysis

Two **simulated** datasets ship with the package so that every function
can be tried immediately: `ncd_survey` (2,400 adults, STEPS-style raw
codes, 12 strata, 120 PSUs, unequal weights) and `child_anthro` (1,034
children with DHS-coded z-scores). They are drawn from a known synthetic
population (`data-raw/`), so estimates can be checked against the truth.
Regions are fictitious.

``` r

vignette("full-workflow", package = "SurveyNCD")   # simulated data, every function
vignette("real-data-nhanes", package = "SurveyNCD") # real NHANES 2009-2010 data
```

The repository’s `analysis/` folder reproduces every table and figure in
the papers describing the package, including a 1,000-sample simulation
study of bias and confidence-interval coverage
(`Rscript analysis/run_all.R`).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Limitations

- **Complete-case handling.** With `na_action = "na"`, any respondent
  with a missing condition gets a missing score and is excluded from
  [`mm_prevalence()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_prevalence.md)
  (the number excluded is reported). No weight adjustment for this
  exclusion is made, which can bias estimates when missingness is
  common.
- **“Multimorbid” is a convention.** It means at least `threshold`
  (default 2) of the conditions you supply. With fewer than the 18 FCI
  conditions this is a condition count, not the validated FCI.
  [`mm_bounds()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_bounds.md)
  shows how much the “don’t know” answers could matter.
- [`who_anthro_score()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/who_anthro_score.md)
  categorises undernutrition tiers only (no overweight category).
- The gradient-boosting module applies case weights only; it does not
  propagate strata and clusters into uncertainty and is not design-based
  inference.
- Concentration-index standard errors treat the ranks as fixed; a design
  bootstrap gave standard errors within about 11% in the validation
  study.
- Validated on simulated data with a known population and against
  independent calculations, and demonstrated on real NHANES data
  ([`vignette("real-data-nhanes")`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/articles/real-data-nhanes.md)).
  Not yet benchmarked against a published STEPS, DHS or MICS report.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Citation

If you use **SurveyNCD** in your research, academic publications, or
policy reports, please cite it:

``` r

citation("SurveyNCD")
```

``` bibtex
@Manual{,
  title = {SurveyNCD: Survey-Weighted Analysis of Self-Reported Health Indicators},
  author = {Sujon Mia},
  year = {2026},
  note = {R package version 0.2.0},
```

# Package index

## Survey designs

- [`dhs_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md)
  [`mics_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md)
  [`steps_design()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/design_helpers.md)
  : Build a survey design from DHS, MICS or STEPS microdata

## Cleaning and scoring

- [`recode_binary()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/recode_binary.md)
  : Recode a messy survey column into clean 0/1
- [`multimorbidity_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/multimorbidity_index.md)
  : Calculate a self-reported multimorbidity index
- [`fci_items()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/fci_items.md)
  : The 18 conditions of the Functional Comorbidity Index
- [`who_anthro_score()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/who_anthro_score.md)
  : Calculate WHO Anthropometric Categories from DHS/MICS Data

## Prevalence and multimorbidity

- [`survey_prevalence()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_prevalence.md)
  : Design-based prevalence of one or more binary indicators
- [`mm_prevalence()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_prevalence.md)
  : Population-level multimorbidity estimates from complex survey data
- [`mm_standardize()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_standardize.md)
  : Age-standardised prevalence from a survey design
- [`who_standard_population()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/who_standard_population.md)
  : WHO World Standard Population
- [`mm_patterns()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_patterns.md)
  : Most common combinations of conditions (multimorbidity patterns)
- [`mm_bounds()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/mm_bounds.md)
  : Sensitivity of multimorbidity prevalence to "don't know" answers

## Inequality

- [`survey_concentration_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_concentration_index.md)
  : Survey-weighted concentration index
- [`survey_concentration_curve()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_concentration_curve.md)
  : Concentration curve from a survey design
- [`survey_slope_index()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_slope_index.md)
  : Slope and relative index of inequality from a survey design

## Reporting

- [`ncd_table()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/ncd_table.md)
  : Publication-ready prevalence table
- [`autoplot(`*`<surveyncd_prevalence>`*`)`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/autoplot.surveyncd.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<surveyncd_mm_prevalence>`*`)`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/autoplot.surveyncd.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<surveyncd_ci>`*`)`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/autoplot.surveyncd.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<surveyncd_curve>`*`)`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/autoplot.surveyncd.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<surveyncd_patterns>`*`)`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/autoplot.surveyncd.md)
  : Plot SurveyNCD results with ggplot2

## Example data

- [`ncd_survey`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/ncd_survey.md)
  : Simulated adult NCD survey (STEPS-style)
- [`child_anthro`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/child_anthro.md)
  : Simulated child anthropometry (DHS-style)

## Experimental

- [`survey_map_indicator()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_map_indicator.md)
  : Map Survey Indicators Universally
- [`survey_xgboost()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_xgboost.md)
  : Train an XGBoost Model with Complex Survey Weights
- [`survey_shap()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/survey_shap.md)
  : Extract SHAP Values from a Survey-Weighted XGBoost Model
- [`plot_shap_summary()`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/plot_shap_summary.md)
  : Plot SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) Summary

## Internal

- [`SurveyNCD-package`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/SurveyNCD.md)
  [`SurveyNCD`](https://stataid-research-lab.github.io/SurveyNCD/reference/SurveyNCD.md)
  : SurveyNCD: Survey-Weighted Analysis of Self-Reported Health
